record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: What is the correct sphaleron-rate and thermal-friction behavior when the non-Abelian gauge coupling approaches the strong-coupling regime, such as α > 0.1, where perturbative calculations are unreliable and lattice results are still incomplete?

evidence.quote: Another regime that is not fully understood yet is the one in which the coupling constant α approaches the strong limit. This is a difficult regime to calculate and lattice calculation of the sphaleron rate for α > 0.1 is an active on-going area of research [235].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite-temperature non-Abelian Yang–Mills theory with gauge group SU(N) at temperature T, with gauge coupling g and fine-structure-like parameter α = g²/(4π). The (Chern–Simons) sphaleron rate is defined as

  Γ_sph = lim_{V,t→∞} ⟨(N_CS(t) − N_CS(0))²⟩ / (V t),

where N_CS(t) = (g²/32π²) ∫_V d³x ε^{ijk} Tr(A_i ∂_j A_k + (2/3) A_i A_j A_k) is the Chern–Simons number. Coupling an axion field a(x) of decay constant f_a to the topological charge density via L_int = (a/f_a)(g²/32π²) Tr(G_{μν} \tilde G^{μν}) induces a thermal friction coefficient

  Υ(T) = (2 Γ_sph) / (f_a² T)

in the homogeneous equation of motion ä + (3H + Υ) ȧ + V'(a) = 0.

In the weak-coupling regime (α ≪ 1), perturbative resummation predicts Γ_sph ∝ α^5 T^4 (with calculable logarithms), while classical-statistical lattice simulations confirm this scaling for sufficiently small α. Determine the correct parametric and numerical behavior of Γ_sph(α, T) — and consequently of the thermal friction Υ(T) — in the strong-coupling regime α ≳ 0.1, where perturbative expansions break down and existing lattice results are not yet conclusive.
artifact.category_tag: Non-Abelian sphaleron rate at strong coupling
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2022–2024) describes the lattice determination of the sphaleron rate at α ≳ 0.1 as an active, ongoing area of research with no conclusive results, and current axion/warm-inflation studies still rely on extrapolations of the weak-coupling result. No definitive computation of the strong-coupling sphaleron rate or thermal friction has been reported.

status_evidence.title: No Warm Inflation From Sphaleron Heating With a Vanilla Axion
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses sphaleron-induced thermal friction relying on weak-coupling sphaleron rate scaling and notes uncertainties at larger coupling.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024, sphaleron-rate-based friction predictions still depend on weak-coupling extrapolations, with strong-coupling values not firmly established.

status_evidence.title: The sphaleron rate in SU(N) gauge theory
status_evidence.snippet: Classical real-time lattice estimates of Γ_sph in weakly coupled SU(N) plasmas.
status_evidence.claim: Available lattice results are in the weak-coupling regime; strong-coupling lattice determinations remain incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Chern-Simons diffusion rate in strongly coupled N=4 SYM
status_evidence.snippet: Holographic computation of the Chern-Simons diffusion rate in a strongly coupled supersymmetric theory.
status_evidence.claim: Strong-coupling results exist only in special holographic theories, not in QCD-like SU(N) Yang–Mills at α ≳ 0.1.
